title: Topological insulator realization induced by fermionic interaction through BF mediators
authors: G. B. de Gracia, R. da Rocha, A. A. Nogueira, M. A. C. de Barcelos
abstract: This paper demonstrates that ordinary fermions, interacting via a BF mediator, form a renormalized structure with non-trivial topological properties. We explore the analogy between the renormalized fermion and a subset of real three-dimensional topological insulators (TIs) in the vicinity of their single Dirac cones. Using the typical magnitude of TI lattice and gaps, we constrain model parameters. The topological structure induced by radiative corrections enters a class of modified Dirac equations, ensuring the existence of helical gapless near-boundary modes. We derive an effective potential for inter-quasi-particle interactions that incorporates finite-size effects in the axial direction, revealing signatures of spin-orbit coupling and time-reversal invariance. Remarkably, particles with different spins do not interact via the characteristic spin-orbit coupling, and a non-central spin-dependent force arises. We also address the behavior of the system in the phase transition associated with the thin-film limit.
summary: This theoretical work demonstrates that coupling ordinary fermions to BF gauge fields induces a non-trivial topological structure analogous to 3D Topological Insulators. By analyzing the resulting effective interaction potential between boundary quasi-particles, the authors predict characteristic spin-orbit couplings and analyze how these topological features behave under dimensional reduction into thin films.
main_problem: The paper investigates how ordinary fermions interacting via a BF mediator can acquire non-trivial topological properties, drawing parallels to three-dimensional Topological Insulators (TIs). It specifically analyzes the resulting effective interactions between boundary quasi-particles.
main_result: The renormalized fermionic structure inherits topological features leading to gapless helical near-boundary modes. The analysis reveals complex spin-dependent forces and shows how these topological signatures can break down in the thin-film limit.
method: The study employs path integral techniques, one-loop self-energy calculations, and a low-momentum effective field theory approach (Born approximation) to derive interaction potentials between boundary modes.
model_or_system: The model consists of fermionic fields coupled to bosonic BF mediator fields. The analysis is framed in the context of 3D TIs, considering finite-size effects via compactification in one axial direction.
key_observables: Gapless helical near-boundary modes, effective potential for inter-quasi-particle interactions, spin-orbit coupling signatures, and renormalized fermionic dispersion relations.
important_parameters: Finite-size effects (compactification length $L$), low momentum transfer ($|\vec{q}| \ll |\vec{p}|$ ), and the BF coupling constants.
main_assumptions: The theory is treated as an effective continuous description, despite being non-renormalizable. Approximations include using the Born approximation for scattering and assuming transverse sector dominance in loop calculations.
figures_summary: Figure 1 illustrates the general setup involving bulk regions and boundaries for compactification. Figure 2 shows momentum assignment for evaluating the scattering amplitude in the center-of-mass frame.
paper_structure: The paper progresses from establishing the full action and gauge symmetries, through calculating one-loop self-energies and renormalization procedures (Chunk 2), to deriving the effective interaction potential between boundary modes using low-energy approximations (Chunk 3).
why_interesting: The connection drawn between fundamental field theory interactions (BF mediators) and emergent topological phenomena in condensed matter systems like TIs is highly relevant for understanding novel quantum materials.

In the center-of-mass frame, particle A scatters from momentum ⃗p−⃗q/2 to ⃗p+⃗q/2, whereas particle B scatters from −⃗p+⃗q/2 to −⃗p −⃗q/2. The dashed internal line represents the exchanged BF boson carrying momentum ⃗q. It is worth highlighting that each vertex has an implicit different structure in this schematic representation.
